title: Abba Binyamin
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Berakhot 5b teaches: Abba Binyamin says, “All my days I took care over two things: that my prayer be before my bed, and that my bed be placed between north and south.” He also says there that if two people enter to pray and one finishes first and leaves without waiting for his fellow, his prayer is torn up before him. In 6a he says that a person’s prayer is heard only in the synagogue, citing a verse, etc. At the end of Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 3:3, Rabbi Abbahu tells them that it is Abba Pinimon’s opinion. Possibly he is Abba Binyamin.

notes.text: “Before my bed” is kept literal rather than settling whether it describes placement or the timing of prayer. Abba Pinimon’s identification with Abba Binyamin is only Hyman’s possibility.
“Before my bed” retains the supplied literal wording; this review does not settle the timing or place of prayer, or identify Abba Pinimon with Abba Binyamin.
